# Polar Alignment for Equatorial Mounts

Point the mount's right-ascension axis at the celestial pole, not at
Polaris itself. Polaris sits 39 arcminutes off the true pole, so center it
in the polar scope's offset circle at the clock position your app reports
for the current time, then stop touching the azimuth and altitude bolts.

Test the result with a two-minute unguided exposure at 200mm. Stars that
trail into short arcs mean the alignment is off by more than 10
arcminutes; round stars at two minutes is good enough for any guided
setup.

Balance the counterweight slightly east-heavy before imaging. The motor
then pushes against constant resistance instead of oscillating through the
backlash in the gear train, and the guiding graph flattens noticeably.
